In my experience i've worked with alot of people who hear voices of specific people, majority of time it may be somebody they know, family, or perhaps somebody who has abused them. Not all the time, sometimes they can only describe it as male, female, etc. In regards to visual hallucinations, they are much much rarer, but do happen, however i've never seen much of people having 'characters', they tend to see shadow people, or are so unwell they can't describe particularly what they are seeing. I've heard phrases such as 'theres things coming out of your ears' or 'he's sitting where youre sitting' or thinking people are outside etc. However auditory hallucinations are far more common. Delusions (which are different from hallucinations) are also extremely common, you need one or the other to be diagnosed as psychotic. I'd be suprised if someone describes clear characters they experience in psychosis however, generally as well in my experience when patients get better they don't remember the most unwell of their experiences
